contentBlocks.title: Swap Your SASSA Gold Card — Black Card Guide
contentBlocks.description: Postbank replaced every SASSA Gold Card with the new Black Card. The final swap deadline was 31 August 2026, and Gold Cards no longer work after that date. If you have not swapped yet, your grant money is safe — get your Black Card now. The swap is free, takes minutes, and needs only your South African ID.

cta.label: How to Swap — Step by Step

contentBlocks.title: Gold Cards No Longer Work
contentBlocks.text: The 31 August 2026 deadline has passed and Postbank confirmed it would not be extended. Gold Cards have been deactivated — if you have not swapped yet, you cannot access your grant money until you collect a Black Card. Do not panic: your money stays safe in your Postbank account and the swap at any collection point remains free.
Why You Must Swap Your Gold Card

Postbank is phasing out the old SASSA Gold Card and replacing it with the new Postbank Black Card as part of a national modernisation of the social grant payment system. The Black Card works at more ATMs, supports contactless payments, and has improved security features. After 31 August 2026 the old Gold Cards will be deactivated.

steps.title: Gather your ID
steps.description: Take your valid South African ID book or smart ID card. A temporary ID is also accepted. You do NOT need your old Gold Card to get the new one.

steps.title: Find your nearest collection point
steps.description: Dial *120*355# on your mobile phone to find the nearest collection site, or call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55. You can collect in any province, even if your grant was approved elsewhere.

steps.title: Visit a Postbank service point or participating retailer
steps.description: Cards are available at Postbank service points inside selected Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer and Spar stores nationwide.

steps.title: Collect your Black Card
steps.description: The swap is completely free and takes a few minutes. No forms are required and no activation is needed — the card works immediately when issued.

steps.title: Check your balance transferred
steps.description: Any balance on your old Gold Card transfers automatically to the new Black Card. Do not throw away the old card until you have confirmed your balance moved across.

contentBlocks.title: The Swap Is Free
contentBlocks.text: SASSA and Postbank never charge for the Black Card swap. If anyone asks you to pay a fee, complete a form, or provide your PIN or OTP to receive the card, you are dealing with a scammer. A genuine Black Card has 'Postbank' printed on the front.
Where You Can Collect Your Black Card

items: Postbank service points inside selected Shoprite stores
Postbank service points inside selected Checkers and Usave stores
Postbank service points inside selected Pick n Pay and Boxer stores
Postbank service points inside selected Spar stores

contentBlocks.title: Find Your Nearest Collection Point
contentBlocks.text: Dial *120*355# from any mobile phone to locate the nearest Postbank card collection site. The service works on all major South African networks. You can also call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55.

Scammers are targeting beneficiaries during the card migration. Remember: a genuine Black Card always has 'Postbank' printed on the front. If a card does not say Postbank, it is a fake. SASSA and Postbank will never ask for your PIN, OTP, or banking password, and no one may charge you to swap your card.

items: If it is not written 'Postbank' on the front, it is a scam
No forms are required — if you are asked to sign anything, the card is not genuine
The swap is free — anyone asking for payment is a fraudster
Never share your PIN, OTP, or bank password with anyone
Report scams to the SASSA Fraud Hotline on 0800 60 10 11 or Postbank on 0800 53 54 55

contentBlocks.text: Using your Black Card day to day

The Black Card works at any ATM or till point that accepts Mastercard, and you can withdraw cash for free at participating retailers (Shoprite, Checkers, Pick n Pay, Boxer, Usave) and Postbank ATMs. There are no monthly account fees, and the card supports contactless payments at retailers that accept cards.

contentBlocks.title: Lost or stolen card?
contentBlocks.text: Report it immediately to Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 so the card is blocked. Then visit any Postbank service point with your ID for a replacement. Your grant payments continue as normal — the money stays in your Postbank account while you wait.
My Gold Card Stopped Working — What Now?

If your Gold Card no longer works after 31 August 2026, that is expected and nothing is wrong with your grant. Your money is not lost — it stays in your Postbank account. You simply need to collect your Black Card. The swap is still completely free and still takes minutes at any collection point, even after the deadline.

steps.title: Don't panic — your money is safe
steps.description: Your grant payments and any balance on your old card remain on your Postbank account. Only the card itself has been deactivated.

steps.title: Find a collection point
steps.description: Dial *120*355# on your mobile phone, or call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55, to find the nearest Postbank service point or participating retailer.

steps.title: Collect your Black Card with your ID
steps.description: Visit the collection point with your South African ID (book or smart ID). No old card, no forms, no fees. The Black Card works immediately when issued.

contentBlocks.title: Still Free, Still Quick — After the Deadline
contentBlocks.text: Missing the deadline does not cost you anything extra, and you are not fined or penalised. Postbank continues issuing Black Cards after 31 August. The only consequence is that your old Gold Card stays deactivated until you collect the new card.

faqs.question: I missed the 31 August 2026 deadline. Can I still get a Black Card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Postbank continues issuing Black Cards after the deadline. Your money is safe in your Postbank account — collect your Black Card with your ID at any collection point and it will work immediately. There is no fee or penalty for swapping late.

faqs.question: My Gold Card stopped working. Is my grant money gone?
faqs.answer: No. Your money is not lost and your grant is not affected. The deactivated card simply blocks access — your balance and future payments stay safely in your Postbank account until you collect a Black Card.

faqs.question: Does the Black Card swap cost anything?
faqs.answer: No. The replacement is completely free of charge. No forms, no fees, no activation required. If anyone asks you to pay for the card, it is a scam.

faqs.question: Do I need to bring my old Gold Card to swap it?
faqs.answer: No. You only need your valid South African ID or temporary ID. Any balance on your old Gold Card transfers automatically to the new Black Card.

faqs.question: Can I collect my Black Card in a different province from where my grant was approved?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cards can be collected from any Postbank service point or participating retailer in any province, regardless of where your grant was originally approved.

faqs.question: What if my Gold Card is lost or stolen before I swap?
faqs.answer: Report it to Postbank on 0800 53 54 55 to block the card, then visit any Postbank service point with your ID to collect a Black Card. Your grant payments continue as normal while you sort out the replacement.

faqs.question: How do I find my nearest Black Card collection point?
faqs.answer: Dial *120*355# on your mobile phone to find the nearest collection site, or call Postbank on 0800 53 54 55. Cards are available at Postbank service points inside selected Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Pick n Pay, Boxer and Spar stores.
